Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming Compensation of Rs.50 lakhs with interest from the date of petition till it's realization for the death of Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda S/o Mutharayappa in the Motor Vehicle accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That, on 08.09.2021 at about 8.30 p.m, Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda was riding bike bearing No.KA02KA7157 from Soladevanahalli towards Nelamangala on Soladevanahalli Nelamangala road near Karekallu cross, at that time, another bike bearing registration No.KA52J8955 ridden by its rider who came in zigzag manner and hit to the motor cycle of Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda.

As a result,
Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Nelamangala Government hospital.
Inspite of best efforts of the doctors therein, Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda succumbed to death on 09.09.2021, as a result of injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioners No.2 to 4 are the children of deceased and petitioner No.5 and 6 are parents of the deceased.

Hence, this petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective counsels and filed their detailed objections.

Respondent No.1 in the Objection Statement to the main petition denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA 52J8955.
Further, it admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA52J8955
Further, it contended that the owner of the insured vehicle has willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Respondent No.2 in the Objection Statement to the main petition denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA52J8955.
Further, he admitted that the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA 52J8955 was insured with the Respondent No.1.
Further, he contended that the rider of motor cycle had valid and effective driving licence and the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA52J8955 was in force as on that date.
Accordingly, the respondent No.1 is liable to compensate.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

4. Based on the pleadings of the parties, materials placed on record this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that they are the legal representatives of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda S/o Mutharayappa died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 08.09.2021 at about 8.30 p.m. near Karekallu Cross, Soladevanahalli Nelamangala road, Nelamangala, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of bike bearing No.KA52J8955?
3.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re iterated the petition averments.
14. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.

Ex.P1 is the True copy of FIR along with complaint which shows that the Nelamangala Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of bike bearing No.KA52J8955 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC r/w Section 187 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the charge sheet is not challenged either by the rider of the offending motor cycle or by the respondent No.2.

During the cross examination of RW.1, though RW.1 has admitted that as on the date of accident the policy in respect of the offending vehicle was in force, further volunteered that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Careful perusal of the spot sketch and the spot mahazar justify the fact that the accident occurred as a result of negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle as the picture in spot sketch clearly discloses the fact that deceased Made Gouda was heading on the left side of the road and the offending vehicle having moved to the extreme right side and dashed to the vehicle and thereby caused accident.

18. Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner No.1 and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending bike bearing No.KA52J8955 and in the said accident, the husband of PW1 had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
In addition, the petitioners have also proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda.
Therefore, the Petitioners are considered as the dependents on the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda .

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 and 2 in the "Affirmative".
19. Issue No.3:
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 32 years and his avocation is shown as Driver under the Proprietor, Vandana Transports Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.

In this regard, he has produced driving licence to prove his avocation, but he has not produced any supportive documents to show that he was earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 17,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
20.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda as 32 years at the time of the accident.
As per Aadhar card of the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda i.e., Ex.P.8, the date of birth of Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda was 20.06.1988.
The alleged accident was occurred on 08.09.2021.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 33 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda to be taken at 33 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
22. The deceased has left behind him, his wife, his daughters and parents.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 6 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid Parimala K.N vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29307646/
6 down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

Made Gowda, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 44,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/ towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
23.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care in her young age, Petitioner No.2 to 4 are daughters of the deceased and they lost their father's love and care and petitioner No.5 and 6 are parents of the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda have lost his love and care at their old age.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
24. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
25.

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 33 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.17,000/ comes to Rs.6,800/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.23,800/ p.m. (Rs.17,000/ + Rs.6,800/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 16.

After deducting 1/4th towards his personal expenses in Rs.23,800/ it comes to Rs.17,850/ (23,800/ - 5,950) and multiplier applied is 16 which comes to Rs.34,27,200/ (17850 x 12 = 2,14,200/, Rs.2,14,200/ x 16 = Rs.34,27,200/).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.34,27,200/ towards loss of dependency.

27. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA52J8955.
It is the contention of the Respondent No.1 that on the alleged date, the rider of the offending motor cycle had driven the same without having valid and effective Driving licence.
In order to prove the said contention, the Respondent No.1 examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.3.
RW.1 has deposed that, the motor cycle bearing No.KA52J8955 was driven by one Suprith Gowda, aged about 14 years and he was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
In this regard the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet under Section 5, 180 & 181 of MV Act.
This fact is justified from the document Ex.R.3.
During cross examination of RW.1 suggestions are made to contradict the evidence given by RW.1.
However, RW.1 withstood during his cross examination to the averments deposed by him during his examination in chief.

From the careful consideration of the documentary evidence available on record, it is evident that the police concerned/IO has submitted charge sheet against Suprith before the JJ board and in the charge sheet submitted to the Court, the respondent No.2 is shown as accused No.2 and he is alleged of offences punishable u/sections 279, 304(A) of IPC r/w Sec.180, 181(4)(5) and 187 of IMV Act.

Such being the case, when the documents speak for itself regarding the fact that rider had no DL to ride the vehicle as on the date of accident, certainly the rider is to be held liable to pay compensation.
In this case, the rider is a juvenile and the respondent No.2 having knowledge of the fact that rider do not possess DL has entrusted his vehicle to him.
Which is certainly the violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
As such, the owner of the vehicle shall be held liable to pay the compensation.
Now, coming to the decisions relied upon by the petitioners in support of their case as noted above, I have given careful reading to all the decisions.

The facts and circumstances which arisen in those decisions before the respective Hon'ble Courts differs to that of the facts and circumstances of the Parimala K.N vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29307646/
9 case on hand as in the present case the issue is regarding the fact that as on the date of accident, the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whereas in the cases before the Hon'ble Courts, the issue was regarding possession of fake driving licence by the rider of the vehicle.

Apart from that, the facts and circumstances of the case before the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision AIR 2018 SC 2662 differs to the facts and circumstances of the case on hand as before the Hon'ble Apex Court the issue was regarding the fact that offending vehicle had no permit to ply on the road.
Whereas same is not the question involved in the case on hand.
Hence, with great respect, this Tribunal is of the view that the decisions relied upon by the petitioners will not come to their aid.
Now coming to the decisions referred by the respondent No.1 in MFA No.3297/2019 I have given careful reading to the said decision.

At para No.28 of the judgment, the Hon'ble High Court has held that; "Learned counsel for the insurance company further placed reliance on the judgments of the Apex Court reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531(National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh and others) and (2018) 3 SCC 208 (Pappu and others Vs.Vinod Kumar Lamba and another).

entities.text: AIR 2004 SC 1531(National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: (2018) 3 SCC 208 (Pappu and others Vs.Vinod Kumar Lamba and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in Swaran Singh's case referred above has clearly held that, mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence at relevant timeNot in themselves available defences for insurance company under Section 149(2) (a) (ii) of MV Act.

It is further observed that the rider of the vehicle admittedly did not possess any driving licence and the owner consciously let him to ride the vehicle and in such circumstances, the insurer is entitled to succeed in its defence and avoid liability.

In para No.105 of the said judgment, the Larger Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme court has laid down the guidelines as to under what circumstances, the insurance company can raise defences under Section 149(2)(a)(ii) of the MV Act and instances were quoted.

In view of these guidelines, it is evident that non possessing driving licence is a valid ground for the insurance company to succeed and in the instant case, the rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.
These observations were again reiterated by the Apex Court in Pappu's case referred supra and they were reproduced in para No.18.

Considering the said aspects, it is evident that the respondent No.1/owner, who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence, cannot take the benefit of his own wrong, and the insurance company is entitled to raise a defence under Section 149(2) of MV Act.

Admittedly, in the instant case, respondent NO.1/insured did not choose to contest the matter and it is evident from the records, especially the reply given by respondent No.1/owner, that rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on respondent No.1/owner himself.
The Tribunal considering the evidence on record has rightly fastened the liability to respondent No.1/owner, which does not call for any interference.
In the decision MFA.7404/2014 decided on 6 th December 2022, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held the same principles which is held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.3297/2019.

In the light of principles held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka if careful consideration is given to the documents Ex.R.3 i.e., charge sheet filed against the respondent No.2 and against the rider of the motor cycle in question, it is clear that there is breach of policy conditions by the owner of motor cycle thereby handing over his vehicle to the person/rider who do not possess valid and effective driving licence to ride the motor cycle as on the date of accident.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
28. Issue No.4 :
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.37,60,200/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.35,64,200/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 3 months from the date of this award.

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1.

2) 10% each to the Petitioner No.2 to 4.
3) 10% to each Petitioner No.5 and 6.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 to 4 are ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.2 to 4 respectively by way of E payment and after their proper identification.

Hence, the age of the deceased Mahade Gowda @ Made Gowda to be taken at 33 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
Upholding objections of insurance company  that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes:

Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.34,27,200/ towards loss of dependency.
From the careful consideration of the documentary evidence available on record, it is evident that the police concerned/IO has submitted charge sheet against Suprith before the JJ board and in the charge sheet submitted to the Court, the respondent No.2 is shown as accused No.2 and he is alleged of offences punishable u/sections 279, 304(A) of IPC r/w Sec.180, 181(4)(5) and 187 of IMV Act.
Such being the case, when the documents speak for itself regarding the fact that rider had no DL to ride the vehicle as on the date of accident, certainly the rider is to be held liable to pay compensation.
In this case, the rider is a juvenile and the respondent No.2 having knowledge of the fact that rider do not possess DL has entrusted his vehicle to him.
Which is certainly the violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
As such, the owner of the vehicle shall be held liable to pay the compensation.
Apart from that, the facts and circumstances of the case before the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision AIR 2018 SC 2662 differs to the facts and circumstances of the case on hand as before the Hon'ble Apex Court the issue was regarding the fact that offending vehicle had no permit to ply on the road.
In view of these guidelines, it is evident that non possessing driving licence is a valid ground for the insurance company to succeed and in the instant case, the rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.
Considering the said aspects, it is evident that the respondent No.1/owner, who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence, cannot take the benefit of his own wrong, and the insurance company is entitled to raise a defence under Section 149(2) of MV Act.
Admittedly, in the instant case, respondent NO.1/insured did not choose to contest the matter and it is evident from the records, especially the reply given by respondent No.1/owner, that rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on respondent No.1/owner himself.
The Tribunal considering the evidence on record has rightly fastened the liability to respondent No.1/owner, which does not call for any interference.
In the light of principles held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka if careful consideration is given to the documents Ex.R.3 i.e., charge sheet filed against the respondent No.2 and against the rider of the motor cycle in question, it is clear that there is breach of policy conditions by the owner of motor cycle thereby handing over his vehicle to the person/rider who do not possess valid and effective driving licence to ride the motor cycle as on the date of accident.
